scene: Three minutes on the mask before induction. SpO2 is 100%, but end-tidal O2 reads 72%.
question: Ready to induce?
options: No: fix the seal, keep going
why: End-tidal O2 below about 90% means nitrogen is still in the lungs, so the oxygen reserve is small. A mask leak is the usual cause. Fix the seal and keep preoxygenating. SpO2 alone can't show the reserve.
pearl: Aim for end-tidal O2 of 90% or higher before induction.
